{{Short description|Mathematical group}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Grothendieck–Teichmüller group''' ''GT'' is a [[group (mathematics)|group]] closely related to (and possibly equal to) the [[absolute Galois group]] of the [[rational number]]s. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Vladimir|last=Drinfeld|authorlink=Vladimir Drinfeld|year=1990}} and named after [[Alexander Grothendieck]] and [[Oswald Teichmüller]], based on Grothendieck's suggestion in his 1984 essay ''[[Esquisse d'un Programme]]'' to study the absolute Galois group of the rationals by relating it to its action on the Teichmüller tower of Teichmüller groupoids ''T''<sub>''g'',''n''</sub>, the [[fundamental groupoid]]s of [[moduli stacks]] of genus ''g'' curves with ''n'' points removed. 

There are several variations of the group: 
* a pro-''l'' version, which is motivic <ref>{{cite book| last = André| first = Yves| title = Introduction aux motifs| series = Panoramas et Synthèses| volume = 17| publisher = Société Mathématique de France| location = Paris| year = 2004| language = fr}}</ref>
* a ''k''-pro-unipotent version, and 
* a [[profinite group|profinite]] version, which is anabelian <ref>Hoshi, Minamide, Mochizuki 2022</ref>,<ref>Collas 2026</ref>;
These versions were jointly defined by [[Vladimir_Drinfeld|V. Drinfeld]] and [[Yasutaka_Ihara|Y.Ihara]].
